title: Wipro Misses Q1 Earnings Estimates and Guides Weak. India's No. 4 IT Exporter Is Falling Behind.
excerpt: Revenue grew 10.6 per cent but missed forecasts. Deal wins fell to $3.37 billion from $5 billion a year ago. Brokerages are cutting targets.
body:
Wipro’s first-quarter earnings for fiscal year 2027 landed below expectations, and the company’s guidance for the current quarter confirmed what analysts had feared: India’s fourth-largest software-services exporter is losing ground to its peers at a time when the broader IT sector is under sustained pressure.

## The Numbers

Revenue from operations rose 10.6 per cent year-over-year to ₹24,478.6 crore ($2.54 billion) in the quarter ended June 2026, according to a regulatory filing. That missed the consensus estimate of ₹24,776 crore compiled by LSEG. Net profit came in at ₹3,352 crore, up a negligible 0.6 per cent from the year-ago period and down 4.2 per cent sequentially. Analysts had expected ₹3,442 crore.

The IT services operating margin fell to 16 per cent from 17.3 per cent in both the preceding quarter and a year earlier, weighed down by salary hikes effective March 2026 and the ramp-up costs of several large deals.

In dollar terms, IT services revenue declined 1.2 per cent sequentially and rose 0.9 per cent year-over-year in constant currency terms.

## Deal Pipeline Weakens

Total deal wins during the quarter fell to $3.37 billion from $5 billion a year earlier, a 32.6 per cent decline. Large deal bookings were a relative bright spot, rising 12.9 per cent quarter-over-quarter to $1,626 million in constant currency.

CEO Srini Pallia said the Americas market declined due to client-specific issues and tech spending cuts in the healthcare segment, though he did not share further details. “Clients are moving beyond technology modernisation to AI-enabled operating models,” he said in a statement.

## Weak Q2 Guidance

For the September quarter, Wipro guided IT services revenue of $2,574 million to $2,627 million, implying sequential growth of negative 1.5 per cent to positive 0.5 per cent in constant currency. Analysts had expected guidance of between negative 1 per cent and positive 1 per cent.

The company declared an interim dividend of ₹2 per share. CFO Aparna Iyer noted that including this payout and distributions over the past year, Wipro has returned more than $3 billion in cash to shareholders.

## Peers Pull Ahead

The miss stands out because rivals Tata Consultancy Services, HCLTech, and Tech Mahindra all beat quarterly revenue expectations, helped by a depreciating rupee and strength in varying segments. “Wipro is lagging its peers,” Centrum Broking analyst Piyush Pandey told Reuters. “It’s possible that the type of legacy deals that Wipro has is not able to generate sustaining growth.”

Motilal Oswal cut its fiscal year 2027 earnings-per-share estimate by around 3.5 per cent and reiterated a neutral rating with a ₹160 target price. Elara Capital maintained its sell rating and lowered its target to ₹160 from ₹180, forecasting a 1 per cent decline in dollar revenue for both FY27 and FY28.

## What It Means for the Diaspora

Wipro’s headcount stood at 243,044 as of June 30, with voluntary attrition at 13.9 per cent on a trailing 12-month basis. For the thousands of Indian-origin engineers and professionals who built careers at Wipro, whether on H-1B visas in the United States or in Bengaluru, the outlook raises questions about hiring momentum and career trajectories at a company that once represented the surest path into global technology services.

The broader signal is harder to ignore. India’s $315 billion IT sector faces mounting pressure from cautious enterprise clients cutting non-essential spending while using AI to squeeze greater efficiency from existing contracts. Wipro shares fell 2 per cent on Friday on the BSE, making it the biggest loser on both the Nifty IT index and the benchmark Nifty 50.

*Sources: Reuters, The Hindu BusinessLine, Capital Market, MarketBeat*
